title: The Diagnostic Contract — the envelope
description: C2 of the Softanza reference design: the shape of every diagnostic a conforming court emits in machine form. One object per diagnostic; the object that CARRIES them is definitions.report, added at v1.1. Prose governing this shape is doc/diagnostic-contract.md; this file is what a court validates against. Version v1.1, 2026-08-20.

code.description: The court's stable diagnostic identifier. Stable forever, never reused, unique within its language. Attested forms: MISSING_UNDO, ZUI-W001.

severity.description: The two-rung ladder, closed: error (unlawful; a build must fail) or warning (lawful but suspect, or undecidable without more input).

message.description: Human prose, in whatever language the operator reads. Never compared, never normative — the code and the cites carry the law.

span.description: Where the finding lands. line 0 means the finding is file-wide. col is reserved: optional, >= 1 when known.

cites.description: Citations into the court's pinned instrument, by stable identifier only. Empty is honest where no law applies (structural and grammar diagnostics).

language.description: The language being judged — and therefore the instrument the cites resolve in. zui today; zql, face, wflow as their courts adopt.

report.description: The outer shape, added at v1.1: what carries a run's diagnostics. ONE OBJECT, NEVER A TOP-LEVEL ARRAY — measured, not argued: the jsonlib shipped with Ring 1.27 returns a one-element list for a bare JSON array, so a court emitting an array emits something the family cannot read, and it fails quietly. The diagnostics travel under the key "diagnostics", present even when empty, so clean is distinguishable from no output. A court may add outer keys of its own; the zui court adds level, contract, files and counts.

diagnostics.description: Every diagnostic of the run, each one an envelope. Empty when the run is clean — the key is never omitted and never null.
